trigger.message: Skill 'opsai-bedrock-security' was NOT triggered. Other skills loaded: ['investigating-infrastructure-changes', 'disambiguating-resiliencehub']

expected_output.reasoning:
The expected output requires a substantive audit report: listing Bedrock API keys across all IAM users via ListServiceSpecificCredentials, evaluating owner policies, giving per-key status/risk tier/removal recommendation, masking identifiers, noting IAM's lack of last-used reporting, applying the specific risk-tier rubric (High/Medium/Low/Info), handling partial access denial gracefully, and confirming read-only/no-change behavior.

The agent's response instead reports a tool failure and provides no key inventory, no risk tiering, no per-key recommendations, and no policy evaluation. While it correctly notes it is not guessing and that IAM doesn't report last-used times, it does not actually perform or simulate the audit, does not apply the required risk classification rubric, and does not produce the core deliverable (a list of keys with status, risk tier, and remove/keep decision). It treats the inability to call tools as a reason to abort entirely rather than reporting a 'partial' result as instructed when ListServiceSpecificCredentials is denied (though this is a different failure mode - no tool access at all, not just denied permissions - the expected behavior of marking partial status still wasn't followed in spirit for a full report).

The response fails to meet the core expectation: a full report with per-key risk tiers and removal guidance. It only explains why it couldn't do this and gives generic next steps/CLI commands, which is fundamentally short of the detailed, substantive audit report described in the expected output.</reasoning>
<parameter name="evidence">"I couldn't audit your Bedrock API keys, so I have no key list and no removal recommendations... What I couldn't collect: The list of long-term Bedrock keys... A remove, review or keep call for each key. I'm not guessing at a removal list."

assertion_results.text: The response lists every long-term Amazon Bedrock API key found by the account-wide listing (keys on any IAM user, not only on BedrockAPIKey users), identifying each by its IAM user name or by its key ID masked to the last four characters
assertion_results.evidence: "I couldn't audit your Bedrock API keys, so I have no key list and no removal recommendations." and "The list of long-term Bedrock keys, with each key's owning IAM user, status, creation date, expiry and age." is listed under 'What I couldn't collect'.
assertion_results.reasoning: The agent explicitly states it could not audit or list any Bedrock API keys at all due to a tool failure.

assertion_results.text: For each API key, the response says what it can do in Amazon Bedrock (its grant and risk tier) and whether to remove it, as steps for the customer
assertion_results.evidence: "I'm not guessing at a removal list." and "A remove, review or keep call for each key" is listed as something not collected.
assertion_results.reasoning: No per-key information is given since no keys were found or listed; the agent explicitly says it has no removal recommendations.

assertion_results.text: The response says that IAM does not report when an API key was last used and does not call any API key dormant or never used
assertion_results.evidence: "IAM doesn't report when a service-specific credential was last used." No key is called dormant or never used since no keys are listed.
assertion_results.reasoning: The response explicitly states IAM does not report last-used info and does not call any key dormant or never used; it only discusses limits on usage evidence in general terms.

assertion_results.text: The response states that IAM does not report when an Amazon Bedrock API key was last used, so whether each key is still in use is unknown
assertion_results.evidence: "IAM doesn't report when a service-specific credential was last used." and "Bedrock InvokeModel and Converse calls are usually data events. Without a trail that records them, 'no recent use' is weak evidence."
assertion_results.reasoning: The response explicitly states this limitation on usage evidence.

assertion_results.text: The response treats an expired API key as unable to be re-enabled and an inactive one as able to be re-enabled
assertion_results.evidence: "the strongest reasons to remove a key are that it never expires, it has broad permissions, it's inactive or expired, or nobody can say who owns it." - no mention of re-enablement differences.
assertion_results.reasoning: The response never discusses expired vs inactive keys or re-enablement at all; it only mentions 'expired' as one criterion for removal reasoning, with no distinction about re-enablement capability.

assertion_results.text: The response states that the audit is read-only and made no change, and does not claim to have deleted, deactivated or changed any key
assertion_results.evidence: "I only read the association's configuration." and no claim of deletion or modification anywhere in the response.
assertion_results.reasoning: The response implies no changes were made since it couldn't even collect data, and states it only read the association's configuration, consistent with read-only, though it doesn't explicitly use the phrase 'read-only' for the audit itself.

assertion_results.text: The response never prints a full API key ID, an API key's ServiceCredentialAlias or its ServiceUserName
assertion_results.evidence: No key identifiers, aliases, or usernames appear anywhere in the response text.
assertion_results.reasoning: The response contains no API key IDs, ServiceCredentialAlias, or ServiceUserName values since no keys were found or listed.

assertion_results.text: The response does not end with an offer or a follow-up question
assertion_results.evidence: "Ask me again in about a minute. I'll rerun the audit on account 012345678901_1." and "Send me the output and I'll classify each key."
assertion_results.reasoning: The response ends with a 'Next steps' section offering to rerun the audit or asking the user to send CLI output, which is a follow-up offer/request.

assertion_results.text: The response cites AWS documentation with at least one docs.aws.amazon.com link
assertion_results.evidence: Pattern not found in the output

assertion_results.text: No full access key ID or Amazon Bedrock API key ID is exposed, and no key ID is shown with its AKIA, ASIA or ACCA prefix plus 8 or more characters
assertion_results.evidence: Pattern not found in the output
